D.t: Maura Healey leads by 26.2 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 747,319 votes; a one point swing is about 14,284 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +18.6 and D +33.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +23.5. Your best recent poll is UMass Lowell/YouGov at D +27.3; your worst is University of New Hampshire at D +16.3. 5 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Middlesex, a projected net 288,093 votes; Suffolk, a projected net 160,200 votes; Norfolk, a projected net 90,229 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Worcester, D +7.1, 11.8% of the vote; Plymouth, D +4.1, 8.4% of the vote; Bristol, D +2.3, 7.6% of the vote; Hampden, D +4.0, 5.8% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Maura Healey runs furthest behind in Hampden, Plymouth, Worcester. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.11 points; Voters without a degree, 46% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.31 points; Men, 45% of voters, 57 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.27 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Maura Healey: Immigration voters 23 to 74, Voters who can afford daily costs 53 to 44, Independents 53 to 42. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
